sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distinguished from all other species by the very long, slender and nearly straight mandibles, and by the short blunt tooth situated near the base of each mandible; the mandibles of A. hartmeyeri are also long and only slightly curved, but its tooth is larger, sharper, directed forwards and situated at the middle of the mandible.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Not recorded in the original (Not known).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and base of the mandibles ochraceous orange; labrum slightly paler; mandibles rusty. Head broadly oval, widest at the middle. Labrum longer than wide, narrowing to a rather pointed conical apex that overhangs the mandibular teeth; postclypeus distinctly bilobed. Mandibles very long and slender, almost straight to near the apex, slightly curved at the tip, with a small blunt tooth near the base, the posterior edge of the tooth straight and at right angles to the axis of the head. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 the smallest. Measurements: total length 5.25 mm, head length (including mandibles) 2.44 mm, head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.13 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.62 mm, mandible length (from the outer articulation) 1.22 mm, head width 1.14 mm, pronotum length 0.37 mm, width 0.74 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original describes only the soldier, records the alate as Not known, and lists the worker merely as a morph without describing it. The heading line was OCRed as "Hamitermes (Hamitermes) exit is Hill" and the synonym line as "Hamitermes eatlts Hill", both misreadings of exilis; the species is confirmed by the author Hill 1935 and the type locality Western Australia: Mullewa. "Pig." is an error for Fig.; "ocnraceous" is an error for ochraceous; the total length printed as "5,25" is recorded as 5.25. Distribution and biology are not translated into the morphological sections.
